problem: The formula says dpi is 'the screen density in dots per inch'. Read literally, a student will use the physical panel dpi printed on a spec sheet. Android converts with the logical density it reports (DisplayMetrics.densityDpi, snapped to values like 320 or 480), which is often not the physical dpi.
fix: Say: px = dp × dpi ÷ 160, where dpi is the density Android reports for the device (DisplayMetrics.densityDpi, e.g. 320 or 480), not the physical panel dpi.

problem: 'The activity window holds exactly one root ViewGroup. Everything else is a descendant' implies the XML root is itself the top of the tree. In practice the layout is inflated as a child of the window's own content FrameLayout, and setContentView can even take a single View, not only a ViewGroup.
fix: Say: the window's decor view is a ViewGroup; your XML root (normally a single ViewGroup) is inflated as a child of its content FrameLayout, and every widget sits below that root.

problem: 'gravity centres a layout's own children' is only half true and clashes with Q4, where gravity on a Button centres its text. On a widget, gravity positions the widget's own content, not children.
fix: Say: gravity positions a view's own content - on a layout it moves the children, on a TextView or Button it moves the text - while layout_gravity places that view inside its parent.

problem: 'layout_gravity centres the button inside the parent' is too broad. In a LinearLayout, layout_gravity acts only on the axis perpendicular to the orientation (it centres vertically in a horizontal row; horizontally in a vertical column).
fix: Say: layout_gravity centres the button inside the parent on the cross axis (vertically in a horizontal LinearLayout), and it never moves the text; android:gravity='center' on the button is what centres the text.
